profilePeriod: Premiership 2007–2010 and 2013; 2006 conscience speeches and explicitly dated later positions through September 2026.
scopeNote: Answers are editorial simulations of documented political principles, not a questionnaire completed by the person. Brazil-specific statements are interpreted in the analogous home-country context. Modern hypothetical technologies require inference.

uncertainties: The profile follows his documented change to support civil same-sex marriage in May 2013 rather than retaining his earlier opposition.
His 2013 PNG policy concerned unauthorised boat arrivals, not all migrants or all refugees. Multiculturalism and border enforcement are therefore represented separately.
The proposed 2010 hospital funding arrangement was revised under Gillard; it evidences Rudd policy preferences, not the current healthcare system.
The original NBN proposal included majority public ownership during construction and a later sell-down. It is not evidence for permanent state ownership of every strategic company.
The September 2026 industrial-policy proposals update the career profile: international investment and trade coexist with support for sovereign manufacturing capacities.
His preference for human oversight of military AI constrains the bundled autonomous-weapons question. Enthusiasm for AI is not endorsement of uncontrolled deployment.
The mandatory internet filter is recorded as a proposal; no claim is made that it was implemented as originally designed.

Mandatory vaccination, forced phone unlocking, facial recognition, cryptocurrency, cultured meat, brain implants and several contemporary moral questions lack direct evidence. Answers are bounded editorial inference or neutral, not quotations.
RU486 support concerned which regulator should assess a drug under existing law; it does not establish that Rudd regarded every abortion as morally unobjectionable.

Assisted-dying reservations are based on his 2017 concerns reproduced in a WA parliamentary report. The 2006 cloning opposition is historically dated and does not imply opposition to all biotechnology.
The National Archives in-office summary includes chronological errors in some overseas-travel dates; these dates are not reproduced or relied upon.
Claims in partisan speeches about opponents, military statistics or AI incidents are not independently asserted as facts in the profile.
distinctions: The profile combines Keynesian economic management with explicit support for Reserve Bank independence.
Compared with Keating, Rudd supports AUKUS and stronger collective regional deterrence, and places greater recent emphasis on industrial policy.
Christian social ethics and later marriage equality coexist; he is neither modelled as a secular progressive on every issue nor as an opponent of all social reform.
Multicultural public identity is retained alongside the restrictive 2013 asylum settlement policy.
